post.caption: Hatpins got their own city laws. From about 1890 into the 1920s, big hats needed long pins. Some hatpins grew to about a foot long. Heads came in enamel and glass, and butterflies were a favorite shape. The Merry Widow hat was nearly two feet wide, or more. In 1910 Chicago passed a law on hatpins. A pin could stick out only half an inch past the crown. An alderman said women could wear carrots and roosters if they liked. Point protectors sold by the thousands within days. Bits of potato also served as point covers.
